note: Proved the negative that no spiking silicon runs LLM-scale workloads (published SOTA: 370M-param MatMul-free model on Loihi 2, preliminary, 2-3x vs edge GPU), Intel's 15 TOPS/W and SpiNNcloud's 18x are workload-shaped claims (10:1-pruned 8-bit MLP, 'Results may vary'), the only civilian-buyable option is BrainChip's $289 in-stock AKD1000 PCIe board, and the named bridge verdict is NO for 2026 with three revisit triggers.
decision_changed: Estate hardware ledger 2026: neuromorphic/spiking-silicon spend closed to NO (research-grade only; Loihi 2 = free INRC research membership, not buyable; Hala Point = Sandia research prototype; SpiNNcloud = enterprise contact sales; Tianjic = unbuyable prototype; Akida = $289 buyable but edge-class and no estate organ has an edge-watts constraint). Revisit triggers named in receipt: a 10B+ param LLM end-to-end on spiking silicon, SpiNNcloud self-serve pricing, or a chartered always-on edge sensor organ (then: one $289 AKD1000 pilot with measured milliwatts).

rows.claim: Hala Point (announced 2024-04-17, deployed at Sandia): 1,152 Loihi 2 processors on Intel 4, 1.15B neurons, 128B synapses, 140,544 cores, 2,600W max, a research prototype with no purchase path; Loihi 2 carries 1M neurons per chip (Sandia) and the largest Intel research board (Kapoho Point, 8 chips) enables up to one billion parameters.
rows.quote: 1,152 Loihi 2 processors produced on Intel 4 process node in a six-rack-unit data center chassis
rows.steal: Cite this register instead of press hype next time brain-inspired hardware surfaces in a frontier digest; landing spot already filed at watch/inbox/spiking_wide/neuromorphic-hardware.md REGISTER section.
rows.falsifier: Loihi 2 or a successor appears for retail purchase, or a Hala Point-class system serves production non-research inference.

rows.claim: The headline 15 TOPS/W and 100x-less-energy claims are workload-shaped: measured on a 14,784-layer 8-bit MLP pruned 10:1 sparse with Intel's own 'Results may vary' caveat, while measured academic deltas on LLM-shaped workloads are 2-3x vs an edge GPU (370M params, preliminary), and SpiNNcloud's homepage 18x-vs-GPU claim carries no methodology at all.
rows.quote: an efficiency exceeding 15 trillion 8-bit operations per second per watt (TOPS/W)
rows.steal: Ban naked multiplier quotes in future hardware digests: require the workload footnote (10:1-pruned MLP, 'Based on preliminary results') on any 15 TOPS/W, 100x, or 18x citation; caveat law recorded in the receipt's ENERGY section.
rows.falsifier: A peer-reviewed benchmark shows order-of-magnitude energy wins for dense, unpruned, LLM-scale workloads on spiking silicon.

rows.claim: Proved negative: the largest LLM-architecture model published on any spiking silicon is a 370M-parameter MatMul-free model on Loihi 2 (ICLR 2025, 'Based on preliminary results'), roughly three orders of magnitude below 2026 frontier LLMs; no 10B+ parameter LLM end-to-end on spiking silicon was found this dig.
rows.quote: we report up to 3x higher throughput with 2x less energy, compared to transformer-based LLMs on an edge GPU
rows.steal: Bank the standing rebuttal line for brain-inspired-hardware memes: 'spiking-silicon LLM SOTA is 370M params, ICLR 2025'; it lives in the receipt's LLM-SCALE section for reuse in one seat, one sitting.
rows.falsifier: A peer-reviewed paper runs a 10B-or-larger parameter LLM end-to-end on spiking silicon with published per-token energy.

rows.claim: SpiNNaker 2's chip is 152 Arm-M4f processing elements with 128 kB SRAM each, and its state-of-the-art language model is an EGRU billed as the first LM on a neuromorphic device, reaching LSTM parity with LLM level still framed as future work; commercial access is SpiNNcloud contact-sales (email only, no public price, homepage efficiency claims without methodology).
rows.quote: setting the stage for taking task performance to the level of large language models
rows.steal: No estate action this year: file and forget; if SpiNNcloud ever publishes self-serve pricing, re-dig the rental path (trigger named in the receipt).
rows.falsifier: A spiking-silicon language model reaches published LLM-benchmark parity, or SpiNNcloud lists self-serve rental pricing.

rows.claim: Akida is the only civilian-buyable spiking-class silicon of the four: AKD1000 PCIe board at $289.00 excl. tax, in stock at BrainChip's shop, but the shop page carries no power figures, so milliwatt-class power claims remain UNVERIFIED, and Akida targets edge CNN-conversion workloads the estate does not host.
rows.quote: Compact, high-performance AKD1000 PCIe development board that drops into a standard PCIe slot to accelerate edge AI
rows.steal: Hold the single falsifiable pilot: if an always-on edge sensor organ is ever chartered, buy one $289 AKD1000 PCIe board, benchmark keyword/event spotting, and bank measured milliwatts into this receipt.
rows.falsifier: Measured milliwatt-class power on a real estate-relevant workload (keyword or event spotting) on an AKD1000 board.

rows.claim: Tianjic remains a research prototype: 28nm proof-of-concept, ~40k neurons, 10M synapses, about 1W, Tsinghua's Luping Shi team, with no purchase or access pathway on the reference page and only a secondary-source enterprise channel (Lynxi spinoff).
rows.quote: A proof-of-concept 28nm prototype chip was fabricated
rows.steal: Ignore Tianjic as an estate option permanently unless a retail or dev-kit listing appears (trigger recorded in the receipt).
rows.falsifier: A retail or dev-kit purchase path for Tianjic or Lynxi chips appears.

rows.claim: Named bridge verdict: NO for 2026. No spiking-silicon path serves an estate organ: Loihi 2 is free INRC research membership (not buyable), Hala Point is a Sandia research prototype, SpiNNcloud is enterprise contact sales, Tianjic is unbuyable, and Akida at $289 attacks edge watts, a constraint no estate organ (embeddings, event detection, drift sensors) has; revisit triggers are named in the receipt.
rows.quote: Membership is free and open to all qualified groups
rows.steal: Close 2026 neuromorphic spend to NO in the operator decision ledger and hold the three named revisit triggers (10B+ LLM on spiking silicon; SpiNNcloud self-serve; chartered edge-sensor organ) against future frontier digests.
rows.falsifier: Any one of: a 10B+ param LLM runs end-to-end on spiking silicon; SpiNNcloud opens self-serve access; or the estate charters an always-on edge sensor organ with a milliwatt budget.
